passages.text: For these two things are, as it were, at opposite poles—good fortune and good sense; that is why we are wiser when in the midst of adversity. It is prosperity that takes away righteousness.
passages.note: Adversity teaches wisdom; success can corrupt

passages.text: We often want one thing and pray for another, not telling the truth even to the gods, while the gods either do not hearken, or else take pity on us.
passages.note: Not being honest about what we want
